Corinne Cross's Dead & Breakfast is a cute, wholesome, short (ca. 3 hours) narrative game, presented in a 2D side-view perspective, with mild resource management and puzzle elements.

[h2]1. Story & Setting[/h2]
You reluctantly agree to tend to the house of an elderly lady whose son (a schoolmate of yours) has died, and who has to spend a week in a hospital. You soon notice that the house, a retired bed-and-breakfast, is occupied by several ghosts. Over the course of 7 in-game days, you learn the ghosts' stories and have opportunities to help them transition into the afterlife. In the process, you also develop gardening and cooking skills.

The story is told in a relaxed, empathic, thoughtful way and generally nicely written - it's noticeable that that the developer is a native speaker with good command of her language. The small cast of characters (4 ghosts, 2 shopkeepers, the elderly lady, a neighbor, and the protagonist) is distinct and lovingly designed, I could relate to their feelings and understand their dilemmas. The story arcs are fairly linear, but your actions will determine whether or not you can get the "best ending" for each of the NPCs.

[h2]2. Gameplay & Mechanics[/h2]
You'll spend most of your time reading and clicking through various conversations, with a few rare occasions where your decision can influence the further path of an NPC.

In addition to the narrative gameplay, the game also has gardening and cooking mechanics, but they are held very simple. You can only grow one type of flowers in your garden, and all you have to do is putting dirt and seeds in a pot, which you then need to water on two different days. For cooking, you need to learn a recipe (these are either hidden around the house, or given as quest rewards), buy the ingredients from a grocery store, and play a color-coded "press the key at the right time" minigame.

Since all of the ghosts' story arcs require items that can only be bought at the grocery store, you'll need to generate some money, which you do by selling grown flowers to the florist. This gameplay element, together with the 7-day limit, introduces a mild resource management challenge - but with a bit of forethought, I found it pretty easy to accrue all the money I needed. The game is fairly easy in general and I had no trouble getting the "best ending" for each NPC in my first playthrough. There is a "New Game+" mode that is supposedly a bit more challenging and also includes additional content, but while I did enjoy the story, I doubt that it has enough variation to make replaying it so soon enjoyable for me, so I did not do that yet.

[h2]3. Graphics & Presentation[/h2]
The game uses a 2D side-view with occasional sidescrolling for ther larger rooms. Graphics are stylized and very lo-fi, but get the job done. Soft, relaxed background music as well as occasional sound effects support the atmosphere. The game does not have any voice-acting, and while that may have helped giving the characters even more personality, they are generally written well enough to make VA unnecessary.

While the game generally has rather low production levels, all artistic elements fit together nicely, and no part was detrimental to my enjoyment. A few details (like the lighting differences between day and night, or the reward splash-screens for most characters) are done quite nicely.

[h2]4. Usability & Accessibility[/h2]
The game's settings consist of 4 volume settings, an "always dash" toggle, and a very comfortable key rebinding system. Instead of listing actions and letting you assign one or two keys to each of them, it displays a keyboard and lets assign any action to any key. You could, if you wanted, assign the "inventory" function to more than 50 different keys. This system unfortunately also has a downside - since the displayed keyboards only offers the US ASCII layout, there is no way to assign functions to language-specific keys that do not exist in that layout. Nevertheless, this system should cover more than 95% of cases where players want or need to rebind their keys, and it's very nice that this single indie developer invested the time and effort to provide an important feature that many triple-A products in this genre neglect.

The game starts in a small window that you can maximize, but there is no fullscreen (or borderless windowed) view available.

The UI is generally clear and intuitive, and most of it (though not all) can be navigated with the mouse. Unfortunately, contrary to point-and-click adventures, the mouse cannot be used to move around or interact with objects. For the latter, you have to approach the object and face it, then press the "interact" key or use an inventory item. This feels rather clunky compared to mouse controls, but didn't cause any problems in my playthrough.

The game provides 9 save slots, but can only be saved in one specific room. Thankfully, saving does not automatically end the day or night. Time does not progress automatically, and there's no hurry except in 3 specific scenes when you're playing hide-and-seek with one of the ghosts.

The fact that I never ran into any bugs adds to the impression of a well-polished product that was designed with care for the user experience.

On a side note, the game is completely free of scares, gore, and vulgar language. It manages to keep a positive outlook despite (obviously) having sad or melancholic parts in most of its stories. With its careful handling of its difficult main theme, it might offer a fine way to introduce the topic of death to young ones.

[h2]5. Conclusion[/h2]
I recommend Corinne Cross's Dead & Breakfast to players who appreciate relaxed, empathic ghost stories. It's very short, but well worth its low cost.

[i]Corinne Cross’s Dead & Breakfast[/i] is a very pleasant surprise. You play as Corinne, a young woman who is housesitting a Bed&Breakfast for the mother of a friend who recently passed away. It turns out said B&B is not as empty as she thinks it is…
It’s a pretty short game that deals with themes of grief, friendship and companionship, and the importance of little gestures of kindness in an often unjust world. The art style is fairly simple but pretty, the CGs very nice to look at, and while 80% of the game consists in exploring and talking to the characters, there are some nice mini-games centered around cooking and gardening that give it some additional rhythm.
Overall [i]Corinne Cross[/i] is very chill but also heartfelt and I think the game deals very well with heavy themes in a light but non-superficial way. Also liked the NG+ mode which is essentially a retelling of the same story but with additional scenes and dialogue and some bonuses if you explore the house and its surroundings at the right time.
I was charmed by [i]Corinne Cross’s Dead & Breakfast[/i]. It's pretty much the antithesis of a horror game and while it is not overtly ambitious it does hits the right notes for everything it sets out to do. The price is really perfect for what you get in this experience, and I can't recommend it enough to people who enjoy story-driven games. I’m really looking forward to the developer’s next game!

This is a wonderful and very heart-warming game. The story is delightful, telling of Corinne's coming to terms with her status as a medium to the ghostly inhabitants of the B&B she finds herself taking care of for a week. In that time, you are tasked with taking care of said ghosts by looking after their needs, each in a slightly different way. There is an "action point management" element to it, as everything makes the player character more tired, but I never went below 50% in my standard play - I believe NG+ is harder.  I completed a "standard" game in just under 2.5 hours, with New Game+ mode opening up after that, so I suspect the game is 100%able in about 5-6 hours.

The game is consistently upbeat and, as it says, not scary. It does take some fairly heavy subject matter and slide over it a little freely, but that suits the nature of what the game wants to be.

The art style is great, and the music is perfect for the length of the game. I also think the controls have been updated since some reviews, as I had no difficulty with them. The only thing that seemed a little odd to me is that one of the later rooms that you can unlock has an exit that is different to that which you expect, and I found myself entering (or trying to enter) another room more often than leaving the room itself. I understand the design choice, but in a game I find little issue with, it was oddly frustrating.

I highly recommend this game, and hope that you get the same enjoyment from it that I did.

Corinne Cross's Dead & Breakfast is a little point and click adventure where you play Corrine, who is house sitting what used to be a bed and breakfast. She is an insomniac and divides her odd day/night awake time between the locals of this little town and the ghosts who show up after her first night.

Charming graphics make this little story very endearing. It was a slight adjustment to get used to keyboard only controls and figuring out how to deal with the game's resolution (you can change it in-game by looking and Corinne's laptop). But it is a simple set up which does not take any kind of fast reaction time or anything like that. And if you've played other keyboard control/RPGmaker games you will already be used to it. 

Story-wise I want to give this game ten gold stars. There's no sarcasm or trying to be edgy, it's just people saying their thoughts and trying to do their best when faced with one of the hardest subjects any of us will have to deal with: death. The NPCs gave a surprisingly heartfelt performance and you'll find smiles and tears here in a way that few if any video games can pull off.

I hope the people behind this game can keep making wonderful things like CCD&B. I definitely recommend this game, it's worth the full price tag.

Corinne Cross's Dead & breakfast is made by Bad Chalk, and is one of those small indie games you just "stumble upon". I loved the look of it from the very first time I found it. I "saved" it on my steam wishlist, and actually forgot about it for awhile. Steam will never let you forget, and when the game got updated, it came back on my front page reminding me that this game existed - I bought it right away. 

CCDB is about a girl named Corinne who just lost a friend. Her mom made her house-sit the friend's moms house - Because the mom got sick and went to the hospital. She quickly found out that this isn't an ordinary house, well - and It's actually also an Bed and breakfast - And for a week she needs to keep it all together. 
She learns that she isn't an ordinary girl either. 


This game was so beautiful and sweet. The style is great and the story is really nice. It's short, yes, and it could be longer - But I liked every day that went buy in-game. I would rather play a short neat game like this, than watch most movies. It was a great experience. 

I actually liked the game a lot more after reading a bit about the dev. It's (as far as I know) made by only one person - Cecilia Bishton - a computer game development student. It's so well done, and I'm really looking forward to try out her other games she is working on when they get released! 

If you are fan of the small story-driven adventure genre, and loves to play indie games, go check out this game!

Corinne Cross’s Dead and Breakfast is such a sweet and lovely game. If you’re interested in ghosts, cooking, gardening, or accepting the existence of death, then this is the game for you.

The art and music are beautiful, perfectly suited to the story. The characters are all interesting and I would have talked to them all far more if I could.

If you want a short (the base game took about 2-3 hours for the best ending) and sweet game to play then you need to get this.

Corinne cross's Dead & breakfast, a super sweet, charming little home. Would definitely stay there whether it existed in real life or even just in game. Enjoyable from start to finish, with many fun, memorable moments throughout. Relaxing and charming gameplay, with an adorable art style and a story totally worth your time. I've always enjoyed staying in bed & breakfasts but now it'll be a little more special each time as i know how fun it can be to host one. even if its for just a week. Not to mention the adventures you can get into and friends you can make in such a short but wonderful time.

This game was so awesome! It has a lot of great story and the characters are very detailed. It deals with greif and loss and carries an overall good message. The art is beautiful. The game + just makes it even better.

This game is a great little gem!  The art is cute, the gameplay is minimal but charming and the music is lovely but what really stands out is the writing.  As someone who has lost a few people in my life (some closer than others), I found the way this story dealt with death and mourning to be really realistic.  From the "sad" messages on instaface, an in-game social media website to the really heavy stuff like a mother mourning her child, each facet was handled with wisdom, heart, and humor that I found really enjoyable.  On top of the deft handling of such heavy themes, the characters were all interesting and I was happy to get a chance to talk to them every chance I could.  I have to admit I cried a lot at certain points of this game but that just speaks to how well-written it was and how much the creator had made me care.

The only slight complaint I could possibly make about this game is that you can't check the recipes you know to figure out what you need to buy without interacting with the stove which uses up some of your energy for the day.  At some points, especially in the second playthrough, you don't really have energy to spare so it's a bit of an inconvience but one that can be worked around easily if you just make sure to write down the recipes as you learn them on a pad of paper.

Aside from this small thing though, Corinne Cross's Dead & Breakfast is a charming game and a genuinely impressive piece of work for what seems to be a basically one person studio.  I can't wait to see what they will come out with next!
Wonderful rpg, emotional and beautifully made, so many routes, plus a new game plus makes replaying even better

A short game about grief and moving on after loss.
The hand-drawn / watercolor-y art style is very charming.

Has a New Game+ mode with extra story bits.

好游戏，开始有悬疑要素（屋子里莫名其妙多出东西，电视自己开起来之类的），后面很温馨可爱，内容是围绕面对不期而至的死亡，该以怎样的态度生活。
       没有中文字幕，但是出现的英文还都算简单，高中英语水平应该就能看懂。
       最后，掉落的卡片巨可爱！水彩风格的那种！完全舍不得卖！

Pros: 
*Music, for a small game it's cute music and fitting.
*Characters, some are likeable, some need to grow on you, some are mysterious, there's a variety!
*Story, wonderful story and in my opinion definitely worth a second playthrough for the New Game+ extra scenes.
Definitely a very different and cute little short game that I thoroughly enjoyed playing through twice in 5 hours. I won't be forgetting this one anytime soon.

Cons:
*I wanted more! xD Gosh I wish it was longer, but for the price it was plenty of content. *crosses fingers* sequel?

I initially picked up this game because I'm a big fan of Blackwell and ghost games really get my engine going.  But after playing it, I've realized this game really stands in a league of its own.  Anyone can tell you that it's precious and charming - I mean, just look at it!  But it actually takes a little bit of strategy, and I couldn't even find all the recipes or get every character's best ending on the first go.  And speaking of the characters, they are all written so well and so human that I was in tears by the end of the game because my heart was so full for each of them.  It's not a grandiose game by any means, but a cozy little trip, and sometimes that's just what I need.
Such a cute little game! It was a little sad but happy in the end :')

pros:
-Pure content... If you need a game that will make you feel good and smile on a rainy day, this game is great. The story is simple and cute and it only takes a few hours to play through it.
-Visually pleasing
-Easy to understand objective as they are pretty clearly laid out.
-Allows you to walk faster... yes, this is THAT imporant. Nothing annoys me more thn a game that forces me to move slowly.
-I enjoyed that they threw in "amount of energy" and money management, it makes you think more carefully about what you do.
-For the price it's totally worth it...

cons:
-Glitchy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ achievments... I beat this entire game with nothing to show for it even though I should have gotten close to all of them except the [spoiler] "10 flower pot"[/spoiler]  achievment. This, was very upsetting for me as someone who enjoys unlocking achiemvents to show for their hard work... Achivmenets validate all the time I waste gaming lol. This was upsetting enough to where I probably wont do the harder mode play through.
-The controls kinda suck and you cannot change them around to fit what works for you. I have a gaming laptop and was physically uncomfortable for a lot of it. BUT, after a while i did adjust/just got used to it.
-If you press f12 the FREAKING STEAM SCREENSHOT BUTTON FOR ALL GAMES, it exits the game without asking first and without saving. This, was, infurriating... As I am also someone who likes to remember games by taking screenshots of the most memorable moments.
Cute game.

This is an incredible short and sweet game. The writing is fantastic and makes you adore the characters with its unique premises. I also enjoyed the new game + mode which adds a lot of replayability with its new story arcs. By the end, I just wanted more. I can't wait to see what this developer can push out.
Got this during the Summer Sale. Delightful! The story is cute, the "best ending" is adorable, New Game+ gives you some extras, and it's easy. Good casual game.

I enjoyed this game. I played it through twice (so I could play the 2nd mode).
The achievement problem persists so if you haven't gotten an achievement for a while (even if you got one or two initially) consider reinstalling the game early. 

Play this if you're looking for a neat little story that will last you 2-3 hours.
Some depth of storytelling, but not too heavy.

A short two hour game but it's really charming
It made me cry a bit, bittersweet feelings everywhere!
The art is really cute too.

I usually do not write reviews. I will make an exception for this game, because it deserves some praise. The game is short,(about two and a half hours to get through the maingame, depending on your fafery level). 
It is Pretty,
It is Sweet.
It is Short,
It has charm.
If you are reading this Miss Dev, I am looking forward to seeing more games from you.

A really enjoyable game, from start to finish. Part visual novel, part time management, with some gardening and a dash of cooking for good measure. It features a cute artstyle and unique design to it, but is also wonderfully written in terms of character, dialogue and overall storyline. This game tackles a heavy subject (the death of a friend) with a lighthearted but honest nature.  Even when ghosts are introduced into the mix, it doesn't feel silly or out of place. Everything just fits together from beginning to end quite nicely in a linear and satisfying way. It also has replay value, since the game is a bit more challenging (with more achievements along the way) if you want to play it again. I would love to see more games from this developer in the future.

This story is so touching and nice.. the ending just made me feel sad yet happy at the same time :'( Though it' only 7 days of journey, it left me in love with his game :') i love this game, totally recommend it! ♥

Super-cute mini RPG with surprisingly interesting characters for the size of the game!  Moving around got a little repetitive (especially because I felt like I needed to check all areas of the house every day), but overall a very enjoyable, heartwarming game.

Corinne Cross's Dead & Breakfast is a charming game with an unusual setting and compelling characters. Playing as Corinne, you find yourself tending to a retired B&B while its owner is in the hospital, and soon you'll find other inhabitants wondering around. 

Completed this game in about 2 hours, although I haven't touched new game+ but from what I've seen it adds new scenes and of course a harder difficulty.

Pros: 

- Cute art Style
- Characters
- Entertaining story

Neutral: 

- I found the daytime music to get a bit repetitive; I feel as though I have heard the same sounds in youtube videos
- It's rather short, which can be a good or a bad thing, I don't mind as the experience was enjoyable enough
- There is hardly any gameplay at all, but I expected as much given the game's setting

I do recommend this game to anyone who likes short but interesting games that have character. I'll be keeping an eye on these devs to see what else they conjure up.

Short and sweet with a cute art style and relaxing pace--if you enjoy whimsy with a supernatural side (with an order of coping with grief) then this is the game for you. I find myself going back to it several times even if it's been completed already on my end. I hope Bad Chalk continues to make games, or even revisits Corinne's world in the future.
